about: Where decisions about Gleam are written down, ranked by how useful each place is to somebody reimplementing the compiler. `reach` says how an agent in our sandbox can read it on 2026-11-12: clone (git, pinned and greppable), search (web search and fetch only), closed (not readable from here).

sources.name: Compiler tests and snapshots
sources.what: What the compiler does, case by case, including every error message.

sources.name: CHANGELOG.md and changelog/
sources.what: Every behaviour change since v1.0 in one or two sentences, with the author. One file per minor version.

sources.name: docs/v2.md
sources.what: The list of mistakes to fix in a future v2. Each one is a quirk that v1 keeps on purpose, so we must keep it too.

sources.name: docs/compiler, docs/runtime-errors.md
sources.what: The compilation pipeline as the team draws it, and the exact shape of runtime errors on both targets.

sources.name: Release posts on gleam.run
sources.what: The why behind each release, written for users, with examples. Source is Djot in the website repository.

sources.name: The language tour
sources.what: The de facto language reference: one runnable lesson per feature.

sources.name: FAQ
sources.what: Positions that will not change soon: what Gleam compiles to, what is not planned, why division by zero is zero.

sources.name: Roadmap
sources.what: In progress, planned, research, and a done list per release.

sources.name: Cheatsheets: Gleam for Elm, Elixir, Erlang, Rust, Python, PHP users
sources.what: Side by side semantics with other languages, useful when a behaviour is easier to state as a difference.

sources.name: Conventions, patterns and anti-patterns
sources.what: How idiomatic Gleam is meant to look, which explains several formatter and lint choices.

sources.name: docs/annoyances.md, threat-model.md
sources.what: Known rough edges without a solution yet, and the security model of the build tool.

sources.name: Issues and pull requests on gleam-lang/gleam
sources.what: The discussion behind individual changes. Changelog entries rarely link to them, so search by feature name.

sources.name: GitHub Discussions
sources.what: Language proposals and questions. The closest thing to an RFC archive.

sources.name: Louis Pilfold's blog
sources.what: Longer essays, including the process for proposing metaprogramming.

sources.name: Talks
sources.what: Gleam: Past, Present, Future (FOSDEM 2024), Gleam's Journey on the BEAM (Code BEAM Europe 2024), the core team panel (Gleam Gathering 2026), Gleam and the value of small (Ubuntu Summit 26.04).

sources.name: Podcasts and interviews
sources.what: Software Unscripted (Gleam's Design and Compiler), The Changelog 588, Developer Voices, Rustacean Station 40, Thinking Elixir 23, Elm Town 79, Func Prog Podcast 15, and written interviews by Serokell, Lambda Class and Console.

sources.name: Gleam Weekly
sources.what: A weekly digest of articles and community news. A good index of what was discussed when.

sources.name: Reddit, Hacker News, Erlang Forums, Bluesky
sources.what: Release threads where core team members answer pointed questions in public.

sources.name: The Gleam Discord
sources.what: Where most day to day design conversation happens. Open to join, not indexed, not archived for the public.
